Naomi / Amelia — I reviewed BBH_Preferred_DPA_redline_v1.pdf. High-level notes:

1) Retention: 7 years as written conflicts with our standard data retention/risk posture and could create indefinite liability; we can offer a compromise of 5 years with a business-justified extension clause (e.g., written request + executive approval).

2) Subprocessors: Their redline expands subprocessors beyond standard categories. We'll accept the expanded language if we can preserve notification windows (30 days) and reasonable challenge process.

3) Liability cap & indemnity: Requested carve-outs around biometric/PHI liability are notable. We'll propose a structured exception limited to proven breach scenarios and capped by the MSA liability cap.

Attached is our proposed response/redline (RI_DPA_redline_response_v2.pdf) — this highlights the suggested edits and a short rationale for each change.

Also: please confirm the signer map and whether BrightBridge requires a witnessed signature for any health-specific attestation.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
Attachment: RI_DPA_redline_response_v2.pdf (pdf)

Team — short commercial context for footprint: this is a pilot with ~200k patient records, real-time ingestion with encryption in transit and at rest. The buyer is flexible on timing but procurement wants signature before the end of next week to hit pricing.

On the 7-year retention ask: BrightBridge says it's driven by internal audit/insurance policy, and procurement prefers not to over-index on exec approvals. If Legal wants exec signoff for 5->7 year concession, I can route to our CRO for a one-time exception but would want a clean ask (summary + risk tradeoffs).

I'll collect the signer list from Gwen and push the DocuSign envelope once we have the final redline.

Marcus
